subject: general
question: Why is the peninsular plateau considered geologically stable?

options.text: It is located on an ancient shield region with low seismic activity.
It is located in a zone of frequent plate collisions.
It is part of a young fold mountain system with active faults.
It was formed by recent volcanic eruptions and earthquakes.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is located on an ancient shield region with low seismic activity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Peninsular Plateau of India is part of the ancient Indian shield, which is geologically stable due to its composition of hard and crystalline rocks that date back to the Precambrian era.
 
• This region has experienced minimal tectonic activity over millions of years, making it less susceptible to earthquakes and volcanic eruptions compared to other areas.
 
• The plateau is primarily composed of igneous and metamorphic rocks, which contribute to its stability and resistance to deformation.
 
• Unlike the Himalayas, which are young fold mountains formed due to tectonic plate collisions, the Peninsular Plateau is much older and lies on stable continental crust.
 
• The lack of active fault lines and tectonic movement in the region further enhances its geological stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major Hill Ranges & Their Peaks**

 
 
• Aravalli Range: Oldest fold mountains; Guru Shikhar (highest peak).
 
• Vindhyan Range: A central barrier; Sadbhavna Peak (highest peak).
 
• Satpura Range: A series of block mountains; Dhupgarh (highest peak).
 
• Western Ghats (Sahyadris): Run parallel to the Arabian Sea; Anaimudi (highest in all peninsular India).
 
• Eastern Ghats: Lower, discontinuous ranges; Jindhagada Peak (highest).
 
• Meghalaya Plateau: Extends east of Rajmahal Hills; Shillong Peak (highest point).
